gaps.explanation: 'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.

gaps.sentence: We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.

gaps.sentence: He isn't old ___ to drive a car.
gaps.explanation: 'Old enough' means sufficiently old; 'enough' follows the adjective, while 'too' gives the opposite meaning.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with rude customers.
There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.

gaps.sentence: We inspected the four bridges, but ___ of them was safe.
gaps.explanation: 'None of them was ...' is used for three or more items; 'neither' is only for two.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ the students passed with good grades.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the + noun' use 'most of': 'Most of the students'; 'most the students' is wrong.
